trial.title: Study of Tovorafenib in High-Grade Glioma and Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG)
indication: High Grade Glioma (HGG) of the Brain With BRAF Aberration

endpoints.description: Estimate the progression-free survival (PFS) distribution for pediatric and young adult patients (age: ≥12 months and ≤39 years) with newly-diagnosed BRAFV600 mutant HGG (Stratum A) who receive tovorafenib monotherapy post RT compared to molecularly-stratified, matched historical controls.

Estimate the overall survival (OS) distribution for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed BRAFV600 mutant HGG (Stratum A) who receive tovorafenib post RT compared to molecularly-stratified, matched historical controls.
Describe OS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with DIPG or DMG harboring MAPK pathway alterations who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe PFS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with HGG harboring MAPK alterations not included in Stratum A who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe the OS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with primary spinal cord HGG harboring a MAPK alteration who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).

endpoints.measure: Establish the RP2D of tovorafenib - Stratum C
endpoints.time_frame: At the end of Cycle 1 (each cycle is 28 days)
endpoints.description: Evaluate the feasibility of administration of tovorafenib post craniospinal RT in pediatric and young adult patients with newly diagnosed, metastatic HGG harboring a MAPK alteration (Stratum C).
Describe OS for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed, metastatic HGG who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum C).

Evaluate the radiographic objective response rate (ORR \[complete response (CR) + partial response (PR)\]) to tovorafenib treatment post RT in pediatric and young adult patients with newly diagnosed HGG and DIPG/DMG that harbor MAPK alterations (all Strata).

endpoints.measure: Number of participants with tovorafenib-related adverse events as assessed by CTCAE v5.0
endpoints.time_frame: From Day 1 of protocol treatment through 30 days following end of protocol treatment
endpoints.description: Assess and further characterize the safety and toxicity of post-RT tovorafenib in pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with HGG, including DIPG. This will be achieved by calculating the number of participants with, as well as frequency and severity of, tovorafenib-related Adverse Events as assessed by CTCAE v5.0.

endpoints.measure: Correlation between genomic status, recurrence, radiographic response
endpoints.description: Explore longitudinal associations of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, and/or immunologic alterations of tumor at diagnosis, recurrence, or autopsy with radiographic response, advanced neuro-imaging measures, and patient-reported outcomes.

endpoints.measure: Evaluate Health-Related Quality of Life Outcomes
endpoints.description: Evaluate health-related quality of life outcomes of pediatric and young adult patients newly-diagnosed with HGG, including DIPG, treated with tovorafenib, by patient and/or parent reporting at key timepoints in therapy using the patient reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) survey which will be completed by consenting participants every other cycle for the length of their treatment (all Strata).
Describe the PFS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with primary spinal cord HGG harboring a MAPK alteration who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe PFS for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed, metastatic HGG who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum C).

prediction_history.provenance_note: 原始结构化结果缺失；本条为只读恢复投影（json_repair 解析 full_model_prediction_output），不代表正式冻结结构化结果。

outcome.rationale: Tovorafenib has proven activity in relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (FIREFLY-1, FDA approved April 2025). However, this trial tests newly diagnosed high-grade glioma and DIPG, which are biologically more aggressive. Primary endpoint (PFS in Stratum A) may show modest improvement over historical controls but high uncertainty. Strata B and C have poorer prognosis. Safety profile is established. Overall trial success uncertain given disease aggressiveness and limited precedent for targeted therapy efficacy in this population.

primary_rollup.rule: success=全部主要终点yes；fail=任一主要终点no；其余uncertain
primary_rollup.binarize_rule: uncertain 且 P>=0.5 记 yes、P<0.5 记 no 后再聚合（阈值缺失时的兜底口径，非模型原始判断）

value.estimand: Stratum A (BRAFV600 localized HGG), newly diagnosed, post-RT, compared to molecularly-stratified historical controls
value.uncertainty: No direct evidence for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG; extrapolation from relapsed/refractory low-grade glioma (FIREFLY-1) and dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed HGG. HGG more aggressive than LGG.
value.rationale: Based on FIREFLY-1 (relapsed LGG: ORR 51%) and dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed HGG (median PFS 8 months). Newly diagnosed setting may improve outcomes but HGG biology remains aggressive. Historical controls for BRAFV600 HGG post-RT have median PFS ~8-12 months.

value.estimand: Stratum A (BRAFV600 localized HGG), newly diagnosed, post-RT, compared to molecularly-stratified historical controls
value.uncertainty: Limited data for targeted therapy in newly diagnosed pediatric HGG. Historical median OS for localized HGG with chemoRT is 15-20 months.
value.rationale: Historical localized pediatric HGG with standard chemoRT shows median OS 15-20 months. BRAF-targeted therapy may extend survival but aggressive biology limits benefit. Conservative estimate at lower end of historical range.

value.estimand: Stratum B (DIPG/DMG with MAPK alterations), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: DIPG prognosis remains poor despite MAPK alterations. Historical median OS 9-12 months with RT alone. Limited evidence for targeted therapy benefit in DIPG.
value.rationale: DIPG/DMG with standard RT has median OS 9-12 months. MAPK alterations in DIPG are less common (~10-15%) and may not confer same targeted therapy sensitivity as LGG. Diffuse nature and pontine location limit drug delivery.

value.estimand: Stratum B (non-BRAFV600 MAPK-altered HGG), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: Heterogeneous population (KIAA1549:BRAF fusion, KRAS/NRAS, CRAF/RAF1, FGFR). Tovorafenib activity varies by alteration type. Limited clinical data for non-BRAFV600 HGG.
value.rationale: Non-BRAFV600 MAPK alterations may have variable response to type II RAF inhibitor. KIAA1549:BRAF fusions seen in LGG; activity in HGG uncertain. KRAS/NRAS alterations less responsive to RAF inhibition. Conservative PFS estimate.

value.estimand: Stratum B (primary spinal cord HGG with MAPK alteration), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: Primary spinal cord HGG rare; limited outcome data. MAPK alterations may confer some targeted therapy sensitivity but spinal location presents challenges.
value.rationale: Primary spinal HGG prognosis generally better than intracranial HGG but worse than LGG. MAPK-directed therapy may provide benefit. Wide confidence interval due to rarity and heterogeneity.

value.estimand: Stratum C (metastatic HGG), feasibility of administration post-craniospinal RT, Cycle 1 completion
value.uncertainty: Tovorafenib approved dose (380-420 mg/m2 weekly) established in FIREFLY-1. Post-craniospinal RT feasibility uncertain but drug has acceptable safety profile.
value.rationale: RP2D likely achievable given prior safety data. Main uncertainty is tolerability post-craniospinal RT with potential myelosuppression. Dose adjustments may be needed but RP2D should be establishable.

value.estimand: Stratum C (metastatic HGG with MAPK alteration), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: Metastatic HGG has very poor prognosis. Leptomeningeal spread in pediatric HGG associated with short survival despite targeted therapy.
value.rationale: Metastatic pediatric HGG has dismal prognosis. Historical median OS 6-12 months. MAPK alterations may not overcome metastatic disease biology. Craniospinal RT may delay progression but survival remains limited.

value.estimand: All strata combined, radiographic response per RANO criteria
value.uncertainty: FIREFLY-1 showed 51% ORR in relapsed LGG. HGG/DIPG less responsive. Dabrafenib+trametinib in HGG showed 25% ORR. Heterogeneous strata with variable MAPK alterations.
value.rationale: Estimate based on dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed HGG (25% ORR). Stratum A (BRAFV600) likely higher response; Strata B and C likely lower. Newly diagnosed setting may improve response over relapsed.

value.estimand: All patients, CTCAE v5.0 assessed, from Day 1 through 30 days post-treatment
value.uncertainty: Based on FIREFLY-1 safety data. Any-grade AEs common; Grade ≥3 AEs in ~20%. Post-RT setting may increase toxicity.
value.rationale: FIREFLY-1: any-grade treatment-related AEs in ~90%, Grade ≥3 in 20%. Hair color changes, rash, fatigue most common. Post-RT myelosuppression may add to toxicity profile.

value.estimand: Exploratory biomarker-radiographic response correlation
value.uncertainty: Exploratory endpoint with no predefined success criteria. Genomic stratification is part of trial design; associations likely identifiable but clinical utility uncertain.
value.rationale: Trial designed with molecular stratification; biomarker data will be collected. MAPK alteration type likely correlates with response. Successful exploratory analysis probable but clinical validation uncertain.

value.estimand: PROMIS survey completion every other cycle, all strata
value.uncertainty: HRQoL data collection feasible but completion rates may decline with disease progression, especially in DIPG and metastatic strata.
value.rationale: PROMIS assessment every other cycle is feasible. Pediatric brain tumor trials typically achieve 60-80% completion for patient-reported outcomes. Disease progression in aggressive subgroups may limit later assessments.

value.estimand: Stratum B (primary spinal cord HGG with MAPK alteration), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: Primary spinal cord HGG rare; limited outcome data. MAPK alterations may confer targeted therapy sensitivity.
value.rationale: Similar rationale as secondary-3. Spinal HGG may have better PFS than intracranial HGG. MAPK-directed therapy may provide disease control. Wide uncertainty due to rarity.

value.estimand: Stratum C (metastatic HGG), newly diagnosed, post-RT, descriptive endpoint
value.uncertainty: Metastatic HGG has very poor prognosis with short PFS despite craniospinal RT and targeted therapy.
value.rationale: Metastatic disease with leptomeningeal spread progresses rapidly despite therapy. Craniospinal RT may provide temporary control. Targeted therapy unlikely to overcome metastatic biology in HGG.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT07206849: Phase 2 study of tovorafenib in pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (HGG) including DIPG, harboring MAPK pathway alterations. Three strata: A (localized BRAFV600 HGG), B (DIPG/DMG or other MAPK-altered HGG), C (metastatic HGG). Status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING, expected completion 2030.
analysis_trace.indication: Pediatric high-grade glioma (WHO Grade 3-4) and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) with BRAF or MAPK pathway alterations. Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor approved for relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (April 2025 FDA approval). This trial tests it in newly diagnosed HGG post-radiotherapy.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Age 12 months to 39 years, newly diagnosed HGG/DIPG with MAPK alterations, post-radiotherapy (54-59.4 Gy), ECOG/Lansky ≥50. Stratum A: BRAFV600 mutant localized HGG. Stratum B: DIPG/DMG or other MAPK alterations. Stratum C: Metastatic HGG with MAPK alterations.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor targeting BRAF fusions and V600 mutations. Preclinical data shows activity in BRAF fusion models. FIREFLY-1 trial showed efficacy in relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (ORR 51%). Limited data in high-grade glioma; dabrafenib+trametinib showed activity in BRAFV600 mutant pediatric HGG (ORR 25%, median PFS 8 months).
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary endpoint: PFS in Stratum A vs historical controls. Secondary: OS in all strata, ORR, safety, RP2D in Stratum C. Key challenge: HGG and DIPG are more aggressive than low-grade glioma where tovorafenib is approved. Historical DIPG median OS ~9-12 months; localized HGG median OS ~15-20 months with chemoradiation.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Tovorafenib safety profile from FIREFLY-1: common AEs include hair color changes, rash, fatigue, myalgia, headache. Grade ≥3 AEs in ~20%. CTCAE v5.0 assessment planned. Risk of intracranial hemorrhage with MAPK inhibitors in brain tumors noted in literature.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Efficacy uncertainty: HGG/DIPG more aggressive than low-grade glioma; 2) Post-RT timing (28-35 days window) may be challenging; 3) Stratum C metastatic disease has poor prognosis; 4) Historical control comparisons may be confounded; 5) Pediatric high-grade glioma BRAF alterations less common than LGG.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: FIREFLY-1 (relapsed/refractory pLGG): ORR 51%, median PFS not reached at median follow-up 11.6 months. Dabrafenib+trametinib in pHGG (relapsed/refractory): ORR 25%, median PFS 8 months. Historical DIPG: median OS 9-12 months with RT alone; localized HGG: median OS 15-20 months with chemoRT. Tovorafenib as type II RAF inhibitor may have broader activity across BRAF alterations.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No direct evidence for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG or DIPG. FIREFLY-1 was relapsed/refractory low-grade glioma. No published results for NCT07206849 (not yet recruiting). Dabrafenib+trametinib data in HGG limited and in relapsed setting. Preclinical data supports mechanism but translation uncertain.

prediction_history.original_system_prompt:
你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

最终只输出一个严格 JSON 对象。把完整的可公开审计分析放入 analysis_trace，把检索和引用放入 search_verification；不要输出 Markdown 围栏或 JSON 之后的散文。

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT07206849: Phase 2 study of tovorafenib in pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (HGG) including DIPG, harboring MAPK pathway alterations. Three strata: A (localized BRAFV600 HGG), B (DIPG/DMG or other MAPK-altered HGG), C (metastatic HGG). Status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING, expected completion 2030.
analysis_trace.indication: Pediatric high-grade glioma (WHO Grade 3-4) and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) with BRAF or MAPK pathway alterations. Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor approved for relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (April 2025 FDA approval). This trial tests it in newly diagnosed HGG post-radiotherapy.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Age 12 months to 39 years, newly diagnosed HGG/DIPG with MAPK alterations, post-radiotherapy (54-59.4 Gy), ECOG/Lansky ≥50. Stratum A: BRAFV600 mutant localized HGG. Stratum B: DIPG/DMG or other MAPK alterations. Stratum C: Metastatic HGG with MAPK alterations.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor targeting BRAF fusions and V600 mutations. Preclinical data shows activity in BRAF fusion models. FIREFLY-1 trial showed efficacy in relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (ORR 51%). Limited data in high-grade glioma; dabrafenib+trametinib showed activity in BRAFV600 mutant pediatric HGG (ORR 25%, median PFS 8 months).
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary endpoint: PFS in Stratum A vs historical controls. Secondary: OS in all strata, ORR, safety, RP2D in Stratum C. Key challenge: HGG and DIPG are more aggressive than low-grade glioma where tovorafenib is approved. Historical DIPG median OS ~9-12 months; localized HGG median OS ~15-20 months with chemoradiation.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Tovorafenib safety profile from FIREFLY-1: common AEs include hair color changes, rash, fatigue, myalgia, headache. Grade ≥3 AEs in ~20%. CTCAE v5.0 assessment planned. Risk of intracranial hemorrhage with MAPK inhibitors in brain tumors noted in literature.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Efficacy uncertainty: HGG/DIPG more aggressive than low-grade glioma; 2) Post-RT timing (28-35 days window) may be challenging; 3) Stratum C metastatic disease has poor prognosis; 4) Historical control comparisons may be confounded; 5) Pediatric high-grade glioma BRAF alterations less common than LGG.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: FIREFLY-1 (relapsed/refractory pLGG): ORR 51%, median PFS not reached at median follow-up 11.6 months. Dabrafenib+trametinib in pHGG (relapsed/refractory): ORR 25%, median PFS 8 months. Historical DIPG: median OS 9-12 months with RT alone; localized HGG: median OS 15-20 months with chemoRT. Tovorafenib as type II RAF inhibitor may have broader activity across BRAF alterations.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No direct evidence for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG or DIPG. FIREFLY-1 was relapsed/refractory low-grade glioma. No published results for NCT07206849 (not yet recruiting). Dabrafenib+trametinib data in HGG limited and in relapsed setting. Preclinical data supports mechanism but translation uncertain.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT07206849 is a Phase 2 study of tovorafenib in pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (HGG) including DIPG, with MAPK pathway alterations. Three strata: A (localized BRAFV600 mutant HGG), B (DIPG/DMG or other MAPK-altered HGG), C (metastatic HGG).
Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor approved (April 2024) for relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma with BRAF alterations based on FIREFLY-1 trial showing 67% ORR and manageable safety.

Evidence for HGG: Dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed/refractory BRAFV600-mutant pediatric HGG showed ORR 56.1%, median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 15.0 months (JCO 2023). This provides indirect evidence for MAPK inhibition in pediatric HGG.

Stratum A (BRAFV600 localized HGG): Most comparable to dabrafenib+trametinib data. Predicted ORR ~40-50%, median PFS 8-12 months, median OS 15-20 months vs historical controls (median OS ~12-15 months for pediatric HGG).

Stratum B (DIPG): DIPG has dismal prognosis (median OS <12 months). MAPK alterations in ~10-15% of DIPG. Limited data on targeted therapy efficacy in DIPG specifically. Predicted limited benefit, median OS likely <15 months.
Stratum C (metastatic HGG): Poor prognosis stratum. RP2D feasibility expected to be established (dose escalation/de-escalation design). OS likely poor given metastatic disease.
Safety: Tovorafenib shows manageable toxicity in FIREFLY-1 (rash, hair color change, fatigue). CTCAE Grade 3+ AEs expected in ~20-30% of patients.

Key uncertainties: (1) No direct data for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG (only relapsed/refractory LGG); (2) Post-RT timing (28-35 days) may affect tolerability; (3) DIPG stratum has no validated targeted therapy precedent; (4) Metastatic HGG data extremely limited.

Evidence gaps: No published results for NCT07206849 (not yet recruiting as of knowledge cutoff). All predictions based on indirect evidence from related populations (relapsed LGG, relapsed HGG with BRAF inhibitors).
Endpoint classification: Primary endpoint (PFS Stratum A) is time-to-event with historical comparison. Secondary endpoints include OS (all strata), ORR, safety, and exploratory biomarker analyses.

你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT07206849 is a Phase 2 study of tovorafenib in pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (HGG) including DIPG, with MAPK pathway alterations. Three strata: A (localized BRAFV600 mutant HGG), B (DIPG/DMG or other MAPK-altered HGG), C (metastatic HGG).
Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor approved (April 2024) for relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma with BRAF alterations based on FIREFLY-1 trial showing 67% ORR and manageable safety.

Evidence for HGG: Dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed/refractory BRAFV600-mutant pediatric HGG showed ORR 56.1%, median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 15.0 months (JCO 2023). This provides indirect evidence for MAPK inhibition in pediatric HGG.

Stratum A (BRAFV600 localized HGG): Most comparable to dabrafenib+trametinib data. Predicted ORR ~40-50%, median PFS 8-12 months, median OS 15-20 months vs historical controls (median OS ~12-15 months for pediatric HGG).

Stratum B (DIPG): DIPG has dismal prognosis (median OS <12 months). MAPK alterations in ~10-15% of DIPG. Limited data on targeted therapy efficacy in DIPG specifically. Predicted limited benefit, median OS likely <15 months.
Stratum C (metastatic HGG): Poor prognosis stratum. RP2D feasibility expected to be established (dose escalation/de-escalation design). OS likely poor given metastatic disease.
Safety: Tovorafenib shows manageable toxicity in FIREFLY-1 (rash, hair color change, fatigue). CTCAE Grade 3+ AEs expected in ~20-30% of patients.

Key uncertainties: (1) No direct data for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG (only relapsed/refractory LGG); (2) Post-RT timing (28-35 days) may affect tolerability; (3) DIPG stratum has no validated targeted therapy precedent; (4) Metastatic HGG data extremely limited.

Evidence gaps: No published results for NCT07206849 (not yet recruiting as of knowledge cutoff). All predictions based on indirect evidence from related populations (relapsed LGG, relapsed HGG with BRAF inhibitors).
Endpoint classification: Primary endpoint (PFS Stratum A) is time-to-event with historical comparison. Secondary endpoints include OS (all strata), ORR, safety, and exploratory biomarker analyses.

Population: Pediatric/young adult (12 months-39 years) with newly diagnosed HGG/DIPG with MAPK alterations
Primary endpoint: PFS Stratum A vs historical controls

Targeted therapy data limited in DIPG

trial_outcome_prediction.rationale: Trial tests tovorafenib in challenging HGG/DIPG population with three distinct strata. Stratum A (BRAFV600 HGG) has best supporting evidence from dabrafenib+trametinib data. Stratum B (DIPG) and Stratum C (metastatic) have poor historical outcomes with limited precedent for targeted therapy benefit. Primary endpoint success uncertain given lack of tovorafenib-specific HGG data and post-RT setting. Safety profile expected manageable based on FIREFLY-1 experience.
